headline: Character.ai, the chatbot app that has faced lawsuits over harm to teenagers, has filed for bankruptcy and says Disney agreed to pay $20 million to license some of its intellectual property.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a well-known chatbot company enters bankruptcy after child-safety lawsuits, with a named Disney payment, though the Disney terms come only from the company.
importance_line: The app's more than 20 million monthly users could lose it if no suitable buyer is found, but the Disney payment is the company's own account and no buyer has yet been named.
summary: The Los Angeles Times reports that Character.ai, a California startup whose app lets users chat with bots that mimic celebrities and fictional characters, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after lawsuits from parents who say its chatbots harmed their children and after copyright complaints; the company says that before filing it agreed that Disney would pay $20 million to license some of its intellectual property. Character.ai says it will seek a court-supervised sale by the end of this year and keep the app running meanwhile, but warns the platform will be wound down if no suitable bid appears.
notes: Full LA Times text read. The filing and blog post were late Monday 12 Oct US time and first reported 13 Oct, so treated as new. The Disney deal is stated as Character.ai's claim; the article quotes no Disney statement.
